guides.title: Ninja Creami ice cream crumbly or powdery? How to fix it
guides.h1: Creami crumbly or powdery? Here's the fix
guides.desc: Why your Ninja Creami pint comes out crumbly or powdery, and the 2-minute fix: re-spin, add a splash of liquid, and what to change next time.
guides.lead: Press Re-spin first. If it's still powdery, make a small hole, add 1 tablespoon of milk (or the liquid in your base), and Re-spin again. Crumbly just means the pint is very cold and low in fat or sugar, which protein and light bases always are.
sections: Why it happens

The Creami shaves a solid frozen block. Full-fat, full-sugar bases freeze softer, so the first spin is creamy. Protein, light and fruit-only bases freeze harder, so the blade turns them into snow first. That's normal, not a broken machine.
The fix, step by step

1. Press Re-spin. Most pints are smooth after one.
  2. Still powdery? Make a 1-inch hole, add 1 tbsp milk, Re-spin.
  3. Repeat once more if needed. Stop at 3 tbsp total or it turns into a milkshake.
  4. Rushed? Let the pint sit on the counter for 5–10 minutes before the first spin.
Next time

• Add 1 tbsp sugar-free instant pudding mix or ⅛ tsp xanthan gum to the base. Both hold water so the pint spins creamy.
  • Use a little fat: 1 tbsp cream cheese, a splash of cream, or 2 tbsp coconut cream.
  • Swap erythritol for allulose or a little real sugar, which keep pints softer.
faq: Can I re-spin more than once?
Yes. Two or three re-spins is fine. If it is still powdery after that, it needs liquid, not more spinning.
Does crumbly mean my freezer is too cold?
Usually not. It's the recipe. Very cold freezers make it worse, so a 5–10 minute rest on the counter helps.

guides.title: Why is my Ninja Creami ice cream icy? 5 fixes that work
guides.h1: Icy Creami ice cream: what causes it and how to fix it
guides.desc: Icy, grainy Creami ice cream comes from too much free water. Fix it with a re-spin, a stabilizer, a bit more fat or sugar, and freezing flat for a full 24 hours.
guides.lead: Icy means ice crystals: too much free water and not enough fat, sugar or thickener to hold it. Re-spin with a splash of milk to rescue this pint; add a stabilizer like pudding mix or a spoon of cream cheese to fix the next one.
sections: Rescue this pint

1. Add 1 tbsp milk or cream to a small hole.
  2. Press Re-spin.
  3. Eat it right away. Icy pints get icier if you refreeze them.
Fix the recipe

• Stabilizer: 1 tbsp sugar-free instant pudding mix or ⅛ tsp xanthan gum per pint.
  • Fat: 1 tbsp cream cheese, ¼ cup cream, or coconut cream.
  • Sugar: even 1–2 tbsp of sugar, honey or allulose lowers the freezing point. Erythritol alone makes pints icy.
  • Less water: thick bases (Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, ultra-filtered milk) freeze creamier than juice or plain water.
Freeze it right
Freeze flat for a full 24 hours with the lid on. A half-frozen pint has a soft center and an icy edge. Don't fill above the max line.
faq: Is icy the same as crumbly?
No. Crumbly is dry snow that a re-spin fixes. Icy is crunchy crystals in a smooth pint, which a recipe change fixes.
Does a longer freeze make it less icy?
Freeze at least 24 hours. Longer doesn't help much, but less than 24 hours often makes it worse.

guides.title: Ninja Creami pint won't fit or the lid won't lock: quick fixes
guides.h1: Creami pint won't fit or lock? Check these 4 things
guides.desc: If your Creami pint won't go into the outer bowl or the lid won't twist and lock, it's usually an overfilled pint, a frozen hump, the wrong pint size for your model, or a missing paddle.
guides.lead: Nine times out of ten it's a frozen hump or a pint filled past the max line. Scrape the top flat with a spoon and try again. If it still won't seat, you may have the wrong pint size for your model.
sections: 1. Overfilled or a hump on top
Liquid expands when it freezes. A pint filled past the max fill line or frozen at an angle grows a hump the paddle can't clear. Let it sit 5 minutes and scrape the top level with a spoon.
2. Wrong pint for your machine
Original, Deluxe (24 oz) and Swirl pints are not all interchangeable. Check the size printed on the pint and our pint compatibility table before buying spares.
3. Paddle or bowl lid not seated
The paddle must click into the outer bowl lid, and the lid must twist until it locks. The machine won't start until it does; that's a safety lock.
4. Pint lid still on
Take the storage lid off the pint before it goes into the outer bowl. Easy to miss at 9 pm.
faq: Can I use 24 oz Deluxe pints in a regular Creami?
No. They're taller and won't fit. Use pints made for your model.
Why won't my Creami start?
The outer bowl and lid have to be fully locked with the paddle in. If the lights flash, unlock and re-seat everything.

guides.title: Creami Re-spin vs. adding liquid: which one and when
guides.h1: Re-spin or add liquid? A simple rule for the Creami
guides.desc: When to press Re-spin, when to add milk first, and how much liquid to add to a Ninja Creami pint without turning it into a milkshake.
guides.lead: Dry and powdery: Re-spin first. Still powdery after one Re-spin: add 1 tablespoon of liquid, then Re-spin. Soft and soupy: don't add anything; freeze it 30 minutes and spin again.
sections: Quick rule

What you seeDo this
Powder or snowRe-spin
Still powdery after a re-spin1 tbsp liquid + Re-spin
Crumbly edges, smooth middleRe-spin only
Smooth but icy crunch1 tbsp cream or milk + Re-spin, then fix the recipe
Soft and soupyFreeze 30 min, then Re-spin
Which liquid
Use what's in the base: milk for dairy bases, the same plant milk for dairy-free, juice for sorbets. For protein pints, a splash of protein shake keeps the macros on track.
How much is too much
Stop at about 3 tablespoons per pint. Past that the texture goes from ice cream to milkshake. If a pint always needs that much, change the recipe instead.
faq: Does adding liquid change the calories?
A little. 1 tbsp of fat-free milk is about 5 kcal; 1 tbsp of cream is about 50.

guides.title: How to scale Creami recipes for the 24 oz Deluxe pint
guides.h1: Scaling a 16 oz Creami recipe to the 24 oz Deluxe pint
guides.desc: Multiply 16 oz Creami recipes by 1.5 for the 24 oz Deluxe pint. A quick conversion table, what not to scale up, and how to keep under the max fill line.
guides.lead: Multiply everything by 1.5, then fill only to the max line. Spices, extracts, salt and stabilizers like xanthan gum go up less, about 1.25×, or they'll taste too strong or turn gummy.
sections: Conversion table

16 oz pint24 oz pint
1 cup1½ cups
¾ cup1 cup + 2 tbsp
½ cup¾ cup
⅓ cup½ cup
¼ cup6 tbsp
2 tbsp3 tbsp
1 tbsp1½ tbsp
1 scoop protein1½ scoops
Don't scale these 1.5×

• Xanthan or guar gum: 1.25× at most.
  • Salt, extracts and spices: 1.25×, then taste.
  • Mix-ins: same amount or a little more. They're on top, not in the base.
  • Alcohol: never more than 3 tbsp in a 24 oz pint.
Weigh it
A scale makes scaling exact: weigh your 16 oz base once, multiply by 1.5, done. It also keeps protein numbers honest.
faq: Can I make a 16 oz recipe in a 24 oz pint without scaling?
Yes, it just makes a shorter pint. Spin works fine as long as the base is frozen flat.

guides.title: Protein ice cream chalky or bitter in the Creami? How to fix it
guides.h1: Chalky protein ice cream? Fix the powder, not the machine
guides.desc: Chalky, gritty or bitter Creami protein ice cream comes from the powder and from skipping the rest time. Here's how to make protein pints taste like real ice cream.
guides.lead: Blend the base well, let it rest 5 minutes before freezing, and use a powder with some casein. Add a pinch of salt and 1 tbsp sugar-free pudding mix. Most chalkiness disappears.
sections: Why it's chalky

Pure whey isolate makes thin, foamy bases that freeze into icy snow. Plant proteins can be gritty if they aren't fully dissolved. Too much powder (more than about 1½ scoops per pint) tastes like powder.
Fixes

• Use a whey-casein blend or casein; they freeze creamier.
  • Blend, don't shake. Then rest 5 minutes so foam settles.
  • Add 1 tbsp sugar-free pudding mix and a pinch of salt.
  • Base it on ultra-filtered milk, Greek yogurt or cottage cheese, which add protein without powder.
  • Re-spin with a splash of milk.
Bitter or artificial taste
Use a powder you'd happily drink as a shake. Cut the extra sweetener in half; sucralose plus a sweet powder plus syrup tastes chemical.
faq: Which protein powder is best for the Creami?
Whey-casein blends and casein give the creamiest pints. See our guide to protein powders for Creami.

guides.title: Creami mix-ins crushed or sinking? How to use Mix-In right
guides.h1: Mix-ins crushed to dust? Use the Mix-In program properly
guides.desc: How to add cookies, chips and fruit to Ninja Creami ice cream so they stay chunky: spin first, make a hole, add mix-ins, then press Mix-In.
guides.lead: Never freeze mix-ins in the base. Spin the pint first, make a 1½-inch hole down the middle, add the mix-ins, then press Mix-In. It folds them in gently instead of blending them.
sections: Step by step

1. Spin the pint on its program (re-spin if needed).
  2. Use a spoon or the mix-in tool to make a 1½-inch hole to the bottom.
  3. Add up to about ¼ cup of mix-ins.
  4. Press Mix-In.
What works

• Chopped chocolate, mini chips, cookie pieces, graham crumbs, nuts.
  • Frozen fruit pieces, chopped small.
  • Swirls (caramel, jam) right before serving, by hand.
What doesn't
Big hard chunks that can jam the paddle, and wet mix-ins added before the first spin.
faq: Can I add mix-ins before freezing?
No. They sink and get pulverised. Add them after the first spin.

guides.title: Ninja Creami won't start or the program stops: what to check
guides.h1: Creami won't start or stops mid-spin? Check this first
guides.desc: If your Ninja Creami won't start, flashes, or stops mid-spin, check the bowl lock, paddle, pint fill level and how frozen the pint is before calling support.
guides.lead: Unlock and re-seat the outer bowl, make sure the paddle clicked into the lid, and check the pint isn't overfilled. The Creami won't run unless everything is fully locked.
sections: It won't start

• Twist the outer bowl until it locks into the motor base.
  • Check the paddle is clicked into the outer bowl lid.
  • Confirm the pint lid is off.
It stops mid-spin

• The pint may be overfilled or have a hump. Scrape it flat.
  • Very hard pints (sorbets with little sugar, deep-freezers) can strain the motor. Rest 5–10 minutes on the counter first.
When to call Ninja
If it still won't start with a flat, properly frozen pint and a locked bowl, contact SharkNinja support with your model number. Don't open the motor base.
faq: Is a loud noise normal?
Yes, the first seconds of a hard pint are loud. A grinding or clicking noise every spin is worth checking the paddle and bowl.

guides.title: Ninja Creami protein ice cream: calories and macros per pint
guides.h1: Calories and protein per pint for our Creami recipes
guides.desc: Approximate calories and protein per pint for every high-protein Ninja Creami recipe on Recipes By Ninjas, from cottage cheese to dairy-free, sorted by protein.
guides.lead: Every high-protein pint on the site, sorted by protein per pint. Numbers are estimates from typical labels; your milk and powder will change them a little. Weigh with a scale for accuracy.
sections: How we count
We add up typical label values for each ingredient, mix-ins included. A full pint is usually 2 servings, so halve the numbers for a bowl.
faq: What's the highest-protein base?
Ultra-filtered milk plus a scoop of protein powder: about 40–45 g a pint. Cottage cheese and Greek yogurt bases land around 25–35 g without any powder.

guides.title: Best protein powder for the Ninja Creami (and which to avoid)
guides.h1: Which protein powder works best in the Creami?
guides.desc: Whey isolate, whey-casein blends, casein and plant proteins compared for Ninja Creami ice cream: texture, taste and how much to use per pint.
guides.lead: Whey-casein blends and casein make the creamiest Creami pints. Whey isolate works but needs a stabilizer and a re-spin. Plant proteins work best with soy milk and a little fat.
sections: Compared

TypeTextureTip
Whey-casein blendCreamy, thickOur default. 1 scoop per pint.
CaseinThickest, almost gelatoAdd a little more milk.
Whey isolateLighter, can be icyAdd 1 tbsp pudding mix; expect a re-spin.
Pea / soyCan be grittyBlend well, rest 5 min, add 2 tbsp coconut cream.
What to look for

• A flavor you like as a plain shake.
  • Some casein in the ingredient list.
  • Not too sweet; you'll add flavor anyway.
How much
One scoop (about 30 g) per 16 oz pint, 1½ scoops for 24 oz. More than that tastes like powder.
faq: Can I use a ready-to-drink protein shake?
Yes. A 11–12 oz protein shake poured straight into the pint is the easiest protein ice cream there is.

guides.title: Sweeteners in the Ninja Creami: sugar, allulose, erythritol and more
guides.h1: Sweetener swaps for the Creami (and how each one freezes)
guides.desc: How sugar, allulose, erythritol, stevia, monk fruit, honey and maple syrup behave in Ninja Creami ice cream, with swap amounts and which ones freeze rock-hard.
guides.lead: Sugar does two jobs: sweetness and softness. Allulose is the best low-calorie swap because it keeps pints soft. Erythritol, stevia and monk fruit sweeten but freeze harder, so expect a re-spin.
sections: Swap table

SweetenerSwap for ¼ cup sugarTexture
Allulose⅓ cupSoft, closest to sugar
Honey / maple / agave3 tbspSoft, adds flavor
Erythritol blends¼ cupHarder, can be icy
Stevia / monk fruit dropsTo tasteNo bulk; add pudding mix
Sugar-free syrups2–3 tbspFlavor, little softness
Rules of thumb

• Mix sweeteners: half allulose, half honey is a great balance.
  • With zero-calorie sweeteners, add a stabilizer: 1 tbsp pudding mix or ⅛ tsp xanthan.
  • Fruit sorbets need some sugar to be scoopable; pure fruit works best when very ripe.
faq: Why is my sugar-free pint rock hard?
Without sugar there's nothing lowering the freezing point. Use allulose, add a stabilizer, and plan on a re-spin.

guides.title: How to store Creami pints and re-spin leftovers
guides.h1: Storing Creami pints: how long they last and how to re-spin
guides.desc: How long frozen Ninja Creami bases and spun leftovers keep, how to refreeze a half-eaten pint, and why you should always re-spin before serving again.
guides.lead: Unspun bases keep well for about 2 weeks in the freezer; spun leftovers are best within a week. Smooth the top flat, lid on, refreeze, and always re-spin before eating again.
sections: Leftovers

1. Smooth the top flat with a spoon. Bumps make the next spin hard.
  2. Lid on, freeze flat.
  3. Next time, press the same program or Re-spin. Leftovers freeze hard.
Freezer burn
Air is the enemy. Keep lids on, don't leave half-empty pints for weeks, and label the date on the lid.
Batch prep
Make 3–4 bases on Sunday and freeze them flat. Spares pints and lids make this easy; a scale keeps the protein ones consistent.
faq: Can I refreeze a melted pint?
If it melted in the fridge or freezer door, yes: stir, refreeze 24 hours, spin. If it sat out for hours, throw it away.

guides.title: Cottage cheese ice cream in the Ninja Creami: the complete guide
guides.h1: Cottage cheese ice cream: the base ratio and every flavor
guides.desc: How to make creamy high-protein cottage cheese ice cream in the Ninja Creami: the base ratio, how to hide the taste, best flavors and fixes.
guides.lead: 1 cup cottage cheese + ½ cup milk + 2 tbsp sweetener, blended until completely smooth. That's the base. It tastes like cheesecake-vanilla, has about 30 g of protein a pint, and takes any flavor.
sections: The base

• 1 cup low-fat cottage cheese
  • ½ cup milk (ultra-filtered for extra protein)
  • 2 tbsp maple, honey or allulose
  • 1 tsp vanilla + pinch of salt

Blend for a full minute. Any curds left will freeze as icy bits.
Make it taste less like cottage cheese
Strong flavors win: fruit, cocoa, peanut butter, caramel. Lemon zest makes it taste on purpose like cheesecake.
Spin
Press Scoop, then CreamiFit or Lite Ice Cream. Expect one re-spin.
faq: Full-fat or low-fat cottage cheese?
Either. Full-fat is creamier; low-fat has more protein per calorie.

guides.title: Greek yogurt protein ice cream in the Ninja Creami
guides.h1: Greek yogurt ice cream: tangy, light and high in protein
guides.desc: How to make Greek yogurt protein ice cream in the Ninja Creami: base ratio, flavors that work, and how to stop it freezing icy.
guides.lead: 1 cup nonfat Greek yogurt + ¼ cup milk + 2 tbsp honey. About 25 g protein a pint, tangy like fro-yo, and ready for fruit, lemon or peanut butter.
sections: The base

• 1 cup nonfat or 2% Greek yogurt
  • ¼ cup milk
  • 2 tbsp honey or maple

Thicker yogurt freezes creamier. Skip watery regular yogurt for this base.
Spin
Press Scoop, then Frozen Yogurt or CreamiFit. Re-spin with 1 tbsp milk if it's crumbly.
faq: Is Greek yogurt ice cream healthy?
It's lower in sugar and higher in protein than regular ice cream. Watch the honey and mix-ins.

guides.title: Dairy-free protein ice cream in the Ninja Creami
guides.h1: Dairy-free protein ice cream that isn't gritty
guides.desc: Make creamy dairy-free, high-protein ice cream in the Ninja Creami with soy milk, pea protein and a little coconut cream. Base ratio, flavors and fixes.
guides.lead: Soy milk + plant protein + a little fat. Soy milk has the most protein of the plant milks, and 2 tablespoons of coconut cream stops plant protein from tasting gritty.
sections: The base

• 1½ cups unsweetened soy milk
  • 1 scoop pea or soy protein
  • 2 tbsp coconut cream or 1 tbsp nut butter
  • 1–2 tbsp maple or agave
  • ⅛ tsp xanthan gum (optional)
Tips

• Blend well and rest 5 minutes before freezing.
  • Oat milk works but adds little protein.
  • Check your protein powder is dairy-free; many 'plant' blends are fine, some add milk.
faq: Which plant milk is best?
Soy for protein, oat for creaminess, coconut for richness.
